chapters.title: Chapter 7: Trading Momentum and Trend Strategies in India

lessons.title: Brokers, Margin, and Market Access for Systematic Trading

children.text: Six chapters have built the theory, the mechanics, and the risk discipline. This final chapter closes the gap between a working backtest and an actual live order on the NSE. The single most important thing to internalize first: a long-short cross-sectional momentum strategy, exactly as built in Chapter 4, cannot simply be implemented in India the way a US-style textbook might describe it. Indian market structure imposes real constraints on shorting that change how the short leg actually has to be built.

body.text: Running a systematic strategy in India requires infrastructure a simple buy-and-hold demat account doesn't provide: programmatic broker access for automation, and a working understanding of exactly how, and where, a short position can legally be carried overnight, since the answer is not the cash equity market.

children.text: Several Indian discount brokers expose programmatic APIs, referenced throughout this course, including Zerodha's Kite Connect, Upstox's API, and Fyers' API, that provide historical and live market data, portfolio and position tracking, and order placement, the building blocks needed to move a signal like the ones built in Chapters 2 through 4 from a backtest script into a live, automated, or semi-automated order. Each has its own subscription terms, data limits, and documentation, and none of them replace the need to understand SEBI's algorithmic trading rules, covered next in this chapter, before letting any system place orders unattended.
The Core Constraint: You Cannot Carry a Naked Short Overnight in the Cash Market

In India's cash, or delivery, equity market, short selling is only permitted on an intraday basis, the position must be squared off, bought back, before the end of the trading day. There is no mechanism to sell a stock short in the cash market and hold that short position overnight the way you would hold a long delivery position. This single rule means a cross-sectional momentum strategy's short leg, built in Chapter 4 as simply 'short the bottom-ranked decile,' cannot be implemented as a multi-week or multi-month cash market position at all. It has to be built a different way.

body.text: This is not a minor technicality. It is the single biggest structural difference between how a cross-sectional momentum strategy is often described in US-centric academic and practitioner material and how its short leg actually has to be implemented for an Indian trader carrying positions for weeks or months.

children.text: Two Real Routes to a Genuine Overnight Short

The first route is the equity derivatives market: shorting a stock futures contract, available only for stocks on the exchange's F&O eligible list, a subset of a few hundred of the most liquid names, reviewed and revised periodically by the exchanges and SEBI. This is the standard route for a systematic short leg in India, but it immediately restricts the short side of any cross-sectional momentum universe to F&O eligible names only, exactly the shorting friction Chapter 1 first raised as a limit to arbitrage. The second route is the Securities Lending and Borrowing mechanism, SLB, which allows a genuine short sale to be settled by borrowing the shares for a fee, available on a broader but still limited list of stocks. Both routes require checking the current eligible-stock list directly on the exchange, since it changes over time.

children.text: Margin: SPAN, Exposure, and Upfront Requirements

F&O positions require margin, typically a SPAN margin component, covering the worst reasonably expected one-day loss on the position, plus an additional exposure margin. SEBI's phased peak margin framework requires this margin to be collected upfront, before the trade, rather than allowing it to be settled after the fact, which means a systematic strategy's position sizing, covered in Chapter 5, needs to account for margin requirements directly, not just the notional value of the position. For the long leg, brokers also offer a Margin Trading Facility, MTF, funding part of a delivery purchase against interest, a leverage option distinct from F&O margin entirely.

body.text: Margin requirements and eligible-stock lists are exactly the kind of detail this course has repeatedly flagged as changing over time, tax rates, index methodologies, and now regulatory eligibility lists. Always confirm the current F&O and SLB eligible-stock lists and current margin rules directly with your broker and the exchange before sizing a real position.

body.title: Can this short position be held overnight?
body.question: A systematic trader wants to hold a short position in a small-cap stock for 3 months as the short leg of a cross-sectional momentum strategy. The stock has no listed futures or options contract. Which of the following is true?
options: It can be shorted and held overnight in the cash market like any long position

It cannot be held as a genuine multi-month short unless it is eligible for the Securities Lending and Borrowing mechanism, since it has no F&O contract and cash market shorts must be squared off same day
It can be shorted only during the last week of every month
Indian regulations do not allow shorting under any circumstances
body.explanation: With no F&O contract available, the only route to a genuine multi-month short is the SLB mechanism, if the stock is eligible for it. Cash market shorts must be squared off the same day, ruling out a 3-month holding period through that route entirely.

body.title: Redesigning the short leg for India
body.scenario: You want to run the cross-sectional momentum system from Chapter 4 on the Nifty 500, going long the top decile and short the bottom decile, rebalanced quarterly, with each leg held for the full quarter.
body.prompt: Based on this lesson, what practical adjustment does the short leg specifically need, compared to how it was described academically in Chapter 4?
body.modelAnswer: The short leg needs to be restricted to stocks that are either F&O eligible or SLB eligible, since a multi-month short position cannot be held in the cash market at all. In practice, this likely means re-ranking the bottom decile using only F&O and SLB eligible names within the Nifty 500, rather than the full universe used for the long leg, which can include any listed stock. The short leg's effective universe is meaningfully smaller than the long leg's, a real, structural asymmetry that a US-centric description of cross-sectional momentum wouldn't need to mention.

body.label: Check the current F&O eligible stock list on nseindia.com
body.description: NSE publishes and periodically updates its list of F&O eligible securities directly, the authoritative source to check before assuming any specific stock can be shorted via futures.

cards.definition: A subset of listed stocks, reviewed and revised periodically by the exchanges and SEBI, that have listed futures and options contracts available for trading.
A mechanism allowing a short sale to be settled by borrowing shares for a fee, enabling a genuine short position on a broader, but still limited, list of eligible stocks.
A standardized margin methodology covering the worst reasonably expected one-day loss on a derivatives position, the core margin component required to hold an F&O position.
A broker facility that funds part of a delivery (cash market) purchase against interest, a leverage option for the long leg distinct from F&O margin.

points: Broker APIs like Kite Connect, Upstox, and Fyers provide the data and order-placement infrastructure needed to move a backtested signal into live or semi-automated trading.

India's cash equity market does not allow an overnight short position, short sales there must be squared off the same day, which is the single biggest structural constraint on implementing a cross-sectional momentum short leg.
A genuine multi-week or multi-month short requires either the F&O market, restricted to F&O eligible stocks, or the SLB mechanism, restricted to SLB eligible stocks.
This means a momentum strategy's short leg effectively has a smaller usable universe than its long leg, a real asymmetry worth designing around rather than assuming away.
F&O positions require SPAN plus exposure margin, collected upfront under SEBI's peak margin framework, which must be built into position sizing directly, not treated as an afterthought.

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not investment advice. Margin rules, F&O and SLB eligibility lists, and broker offerings change over time. Always verify current rules directly with your broker, the NSE, BSE, and SEBI before trading. Consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser or research analyst before trading.
